beats.text: 2PC locks everything. Microservices need another way.
beats.say: Two-phase commit locks everything, and it can block. Microservices need a different way to stay consistent.

beats.text: A saga: local steps, each triggers the next.
beats.say: A saga is a sequence of local transactions. Each service does its own step, then triggers the next one.

beats.text: The last step fails. No global rollback!
beats.say: But what if the last step fails? There is no global rollback to save you.

beats.text: Undo each step with a compensating action, in reverse.
beats.say: So every step has a compensating action that undoes it. Release the stock, refund the card, cancel the order, in reverse order.

beats.text: No locks, scales well. Eventually consistent.
beats.say: Sagas avoid distributed locks, so they scale. But for a moment the system is inconsistent, so you get eventual consistency. Services coordinate either by events, or through a central orchestrator.

beats.text: Next up: event sourcing. Follow for more!
beats.say: Next up, event sourcing. Follow for more system design.
